fichas.title: Archives
fichas.summary: Archives prioritize systematic cataloguing and long-term preservation of written, graphic, and audio media. They may be part of libraries, museums, or universities. Storage should accommodate growing collections, with suitable systems and adequate floor loading. A uniform climate is important; the text favors natural ventilation while noting pollutant risks, and recommends solid walls and simple wall-surface heating where full air conditioning is not used. The illustrated State Archive extension in Dresden arranges archive storage around an access and ventilation core, with flexible room division and rolling storage units. Public areas connect the new and old buildings and include a foyer, reading room, seminar rooms, and cafeteria.
uses: Systematic cataloguing and long-term preservation of records and media
Storage of files, business records, maps, drawings, and documents
Reading, research, seminars, and film viewing

fichas.title: Principle of Source Ventilation
fichas.summary: The illustrated ventilation principle supplies prepared air through shafts and distributes it to floors through ventilation blocks. In the archive discussion, natural ventilation is presented as desirable, but the text also notes the risk of airborne pollutants entering the building.
uses: Supply prepared air to building floors
